title: Japan enterprise market entry ops brief
summary: Working brief for internal enablement and launch ops for Redwood's enterprise push in Japan. Focus: Private (VPC/on-prem) + Dedicated for regulated verticals, plus localized messaging and competitive positioning against global LLM providers and local systems.
audience: Sales leaders (JP), solutions engineering, product marketing, legal/regulatory, customer success
objective: 1) Rapidly enable AE + SE teams to run discovery and proofs with Japanese enterprises. 2) Publish localized messaging and objection handling. 3) Finalize compliance checklist for early adopters (financial services, healthcare).
key_messages: Redwood makes LLM inference enterprise-ready in Japan: predictable latency, strong data controls, and clear unit economics
Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) meet local data residency and audit needs while preserving the same API/operational model used elsewhere
Dedicated capacity and autoscaling let large teams hit throughput SLAs without unpredictable spend — we decouple model performance from tenant variability
feature_highlights: Private: customer-managed VPC with KMS integrations and audit logging — customers retain keys for PHI/PII-sensitive workloads
Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in AP-northeast-1 with configurable autoscaling and predictable latency SLOs
Optimize: quantization and batching recommendations tuned for Japanese tokenization and long-context enterprise prompts
Smart routing: regional fallback policies to minimize cross-border egress while keeping uptime
positioning_notes: Do not lead with model name or openness alone. For enterprise Japanese buyers emphasize operational guarantees and observability (per-route latency breakdowns, token-level cost attribution) and the ability to run identical stacks on-prem or in VPC. Messaging should tie to local procurement pain: auditability, vendor lock-in risk, predictable cost modeling, and integration with existing identity/KMS stacks.
competitive_quick_notes:
- OpenAI/Anthropic: strong base models and developer mindshare but customers raise questions about data residency and enterprise SLAs.
- Cloud providers (AWS/GCP): native infra and marketplace familiarity, but limited inference-optimized runtime and mismatch on rollout controls (our differentiator: opinionated inference runtime + rollouts).
- Local system integrators/players: stronger local relationships and procurement experience, may bundle services. Risk: they can re-sell third-party APIs; advantage: local language support and compliance packaging.
- Smaller inference runtimes: technical parity on some kernels but lack global managed offering, fewer observability/rollout features.
sales_enablement_snippets: Discovery trigger: customer says 'we need on-prem or cannot send tokens outside JP' -> Follow with 'We support private deployments with customer-managed keys and can run within your data center or VPC.'
Objection: 'How do we audit model usage?' -> Rebuttal: 'Per-token logs, model-versioned rollouts, and audit exports are available; we integrate with SIEMs and Splunk via log forwarder.'

Pricing talk-track: explain tradeoff — hosted is best for quick POC, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private for regulatory needs; show simple cost model example for 10M tokens/month across choices.
recommended_assets_for_launch: AE playbook: discovery checklist + 5 templated POC prompts for finance/regulatory use cases
SE runbook: quickstart for on-prem appliance + checklist for KMS/DB network routes
Localized slide deck: 6 slides, Japanese copy + speaker notes in English
Short FAQ doc covering data residency, certification roadmap, and support SLA
launch_timeline:
- Week 0: internal product + legal sign-off on JP offering language
- Week 1: AE/SE enablement sessions (recording + Q&A)
- Week 2: Publish JP landing page and localized assets
- Week 3: Run two pilot POCs with target customers (tier-1 FS and healthcare)
- Week 5: Collect feedback, adjust pricing/packaging for JP market
operational_checklist: Confirm AP-northeast-1 Dedicated capacity pools available and autoscale tested
Validate KMS integrations with AWS KMS in JP region and on-prem HSM test plan
Ensure audit export endpoint and sample SIEM integration documented
Translate one-pager and AE playbook to Japanese and review with native speaker (Kenji)
Legal: confirm APPI applicability and store minimal PII on platform when requested
Support: 24/7 escalation path mapped to on-call engineering in JST overlap windows
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: procurement timeline in Japan can be slow (3-6 months). Mitigation: offer short-term POC contracts with restricted access + technical escrow for assurances.

Risk: local competitors may undercut price with integration bundles. Mitigation: highlight total cost of ownership savings from our Optimize recommendations, and provide SE time to quantify token-level cost savings for the customer.
Risk: regulatory nuance for healthcare/pharma. Mitigation: engage legal early and prepare a templated Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and security questionnaire responses in Japanese.
open_questions: Do we want to list specific certifications on the JP one-pager now or mark as 'in progress'? (ISO/PCI/others)
Should we pre-seed a local partner channel (SI) or push direct AE motion for first 6 deals?
What is the minimum Dedicated capacity SKU we will advertise for JP customers? (ops to confirm)
next_steps: 1) PM to confirm Dedicated SKUs + pricing by 2024-12-11. 2) Legal to draft JP DPA template and share by 2024-12-08. 3) SEs to schedule two enablement sessions in JST during Week 1. Owner: Priya (product marketing).
